subject: SparkStarter credits – policy exception & onboarding runbook
messages:
From: Kayla Park <kayla@olivelabs.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-19T08:14:00Z
Subject: SparkStarter credits — combining promo + accelerator question

Hi Sofia / Ben,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — Olive Labs is excited to move into the SparkStarter cohort. Two quick operational questions before we sign the SOW: 1) We have an existing promo credit package from a previous pilot (internal code OLIVE-PROMO-2k). Can we stack that with the SparkStarter grant, or does Redwood policy prevent combining credits from different promotions? 2) Our legal team asks whether credits can be converted to a committed discount (if we move to Dedicated) or if they expire strictly as usage credits.

We want to confirm the answer because it changes whether we accept the standard SOW or ask for a carveout. If stacking is allowed, can you outline the approval path and any documentation you need from us?

Appreciate your help — Kayla
Kayla Park, Head of Integrations
Olive Labs

---
Attachment: OLIVE-PROMO-terms.txt (txt)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Kayla Park <kayla@olivelabs.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-19T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: SparkStarter credits — combining promo + accelerator question

Hi Kayla — excellent questions, and congrats again on being accepted to SparkStarter. Short answers up front: stacking is possible in specific cases, but it requires a one-time exception and an internal approval runbook. Credits do not automatically convert to a Dedicated discount; conversion requires a commercial amendment at renewal.

What I can do this morning: 1) Share a recommended credit-mapping spreadsheet so we can see how the promo and grant would be consumed over a 90-day pilot, 2) Loop in Finance/Legal for a quick approval path, and 3) If you confirm forecasted monthly token consumption we can pre-authorize an up-to-$10k one-time top-up credit while the exception is processed.

Attached: sparkstarter_credit_mapping.xlsx (sample mapping), and a draft SOW template you can review. Can you send a short note with your expected monthly token volumes and whether the promo is tied to a billing account or to a specific team? That will speed things up.

Next steps I propose:
- You provide the consumption estimate (tokens / month) and whether promo is account-level.
- We run credit-mapping and Ben will propose the exception size and approvals.
- Irene (Finance) will confirm accounting treatment and whether credits must be escrowed.

Cheers,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior GTM, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: sparkstarter_credit_mapping.xlsx (xlsx); SOW_SparkStarter_template.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Kayla Park <kayla@olivelabs.io>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-19T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: SparkStarter credits — combining promo + accelerator question

Kayla / Sofia — looping in Irene for accounting/legal validation. Quick commercial note from Sales: we can approve stacking for SparkStarter cohorts under these constraints:

- Exception is one-time and non-recurring; maximum additional credit we can top up without Exec sign-off is $10,000.
- Promo credits must be consumed first (to keep our tracking simple), then cohort grant applies. If you want the grant to apply first, we need a short justification and product will need to set priority flags.
- Credits are usage credits with a 6-month expiration unless otherwise stated in a signed amendment.
- Conversion into a Dedicated discount is handled at the subscription renewal moment and requires minimum committed spend thresholds (Irene can confirm thresholds).

If you approve the one-time top-up, Sofia and I will prepare an exception approval runbook (I attached a draft) and route to Revenue Ops and Legal. Please confirm: preferred order of consumption (promo first? grant first?), and your expected peak months.

Deal reference: HUB-8472 — I will add this to the HubSpot deal and start the approval task.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Exec, Growth
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: exception_approval_runbook.md (md)
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Kayla Park <kayla@olivelabs.io>
Date: 2025-06-19T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SparkStarter credits — combining promo + accelerator question

Kayla / team — from a finance & compliance standpoint:

- We can honor a stacking exception with two controls: escrow the promo credit (if promotional accounting requires deferral) or add an explicit consumption order in the SOW. Escrow is preferred for larger promo values.
- For the $10k top-up: accounting will treat that as a promotional expense and we will require an internal approval ticket; I will need the sponsor (customer PO or partner sponsor) on record.
- Legal note: we should add an amendment clause that prevents double-dipping into credits after conversion to a committed discount (prevents retroactive conversion).

I can fast-track review if Kayla confirms the promo is account-level and not already attached to another SL. Kayla — can you confirm with finance whether OLIVE-PROMO-2k is account-level and share the original promo terms?

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Kayla Park <kayla@olivelabs.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Thanks Sofia/Ben/Irene — this is helpful. Confirming: OLIVE-PROMO-2k is account-level and tied to our primary billing account (I just attached the promo terms to our internal reply). We are happy for promo credits to be consumed first.

We also accept the $10k one-time top-up while the exception is processed — that will help us avoid throttling during demo week. Please go ahead with the runbook and I will get the SOW signed today (I see the DocuSign link in your note).

Final question: any chance you can include a clause that credits applied during the SparkStarter pilot will not be clawed back if we convert to a paid contract within 90 days? If that requires Exec sign-off we understand — please let us know the expected timeline.

Best,
Kayla
